claim: Model only (F_q[T], q = 5, 7; all squarefree conductors of degree 5 and 7; N <= 3; exact arithmetic; no independent referee). The Moebius sum S_cop(k) of the Prop. 2.1 probe is a polynomial in L_1..L_N with coefficients depending on (q, N, lam, k, number of F_q-roots of F), the same for genus 2 and 3 (1240 vector-strata, 0 off). It is linear in Frobenius traces only for N = 1 (0 of 640 vector-strata at N = 2, 3). At N = 1: 0 <= S^2 <= (g/2)(-D.D)/q on all 5394 L-polynomials, ratio anywhere in [0, 1], equality iff all s_m equal; S^2 is not a curve-independent quadratic form on the Frobenius-graph classes. The graph-class span splits orthogonally into a symmetric block (semidefinite iff s_m real) and an antisymmetric block (semidefinite iff abs(s_m) <= 2 sqrt q); signal and diagonal are symmetric, so the bound reads reality only. Fakes with real off-line pairs pass 96 of 96. No statement about zeta.
errors: No independent referee. REFEREE.md is the author's own check (second implementation at q = 3, 5). J_k itself not computed: the answer is for S_cop inside the round-8 law. The N = 1 test is one inequality per L-polynomial. The tensor-power statement for N >= 2 is argued, not run.
surviving: Lemma 1 in polynomial form with r(F)-dependence on composite conductors; Proposition A (symmetric/antisymmetric splitting with the two signatures); exact exclusion of equality and of any curve-independent quadratic form; three-class fake control in genus 2 and 3.
lesson: The probe signal and the diagonal class lie in the Frobenius-plus-Verschiebung (symmetric) part of NS(C x C), where the Hodge form only reads reality of alpha + q/alpha; the Weil bound sits in the antisymmetric part, which the signal does not meet. A squared pairing equals a norm only in rank 1 (genus 1).
